lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: For more than a thousand years, nothing could break the walls of Constantinople. Arab armies tried, twice. Fleets tried. A Crusader army got in, in twelve oh four, though that one hardly counts, since it was supposedly on the city's side.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then, in the spring of fourteen fifty-three, a twenty-one-year-old sultan parked his army outside them. In under eight weeks, the Roman Empire was over.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Ask historians what broke those walls and you won't get an answer. You'll get an argument. Three suspects. A cannon. A small door that somebody forgot to lock. And one wounded man, carried off the wall at exactly the wrong moment.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The witnesses are not helpful. One is a Venetian who disliked the Genoese. One is a Genoese archbishop who disliked the Venetians. And one is a Greek chronicler with firm opinions about everybody. By the end, I'll tell you which suspect I would arrest. Or why the question might be slightly wrong.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But first, the last night. The twenty-eighth of May. On one of the towers, two sentries are sharing a loaf of bread. Every tower on that wall had two men like them. Let's call this pair Dimitri and Stavros.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: Stavros. Have you seen the fires?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: I've seen the fires.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: I started counting them. I got to three thousand and lost my place.

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Good. Then you won't be tempted to count the men.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: How many men is it? Behind one fire?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Fewer than you'd like. More than we have.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: And how many do we have?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Eat your bread.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Fewer than seven thousand defenders, against something like eighty thousand. And in the city behind them, the emperor was riding to Hagia Sophia to make his peace with God. Hold that picture. To see how it came to this, we need to meet the man on that horse.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: His name was Constantine Palaiologos. Constantine the Eleventh, if you're counting, and the Byzantines most certainly were. Born in fourteen oh four, the fourth son of an emperor, which is not a position that comes with high expectations. His brother John died without an heir in October fourteen forty-eight. In January fourteen forty-nine, Constantine was proclaimed emperor in the Peloponnese. Never crowned in Hagia Sophia, as custom required. Which tells you how the empire was doing.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Nobody recorded the exact words, so imagine the scene something like this.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Majesty, the inventory of your empire.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Show me.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Here. Constantinople. A few islands. And the southern Peloponnese.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: And the rest?

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: That is the rest.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: It's a very small map.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: I could draw it larger, Majesty. It would not improve the content.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The Romans still called themselves Romans, by the way. A thousand years after Rome had stopped being theirs to call. And Constantine had a second problem: no children. Every attempt to find him a wife, in Aragon, in Trebizond, in Georgia, fell through.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Aragon has declined.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Georgia is, ah, considering.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: For how long?

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: They did not say. Trebizond is also considering.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Everyone is considering me. It's flattering. It's also not a marriage.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: An emperor with no heir, no wife, and not much of an empire. But he did have the walls.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So let's talk about those walls, because everything hangs on them. We'll let Dimitri ask. It's his first week.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: How high is it?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Which part?

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: The… wall.

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: There are three. First, a ditch. About sixty feet wide.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: Sixty feet of nothing?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Sixty feet of nobody-wants-to-cross-this. Then the outer wall. Twenty-five feet. Then the inner wall, forty feet and more, with towers.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: And the enemy has to get through all of it.

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Under fire.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: How long has it stood?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Since the fifth century.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: And nobody's broken it?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Nobody. Don't say it too loudly.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: Where's the weak part?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Why would I tell you that?

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: Because I'm standing on it?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Down there. Where the little river cuts through. The Lycus. The soft part. The Greeks call it the Mesoteichion.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: What does that mean?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: "Middle wall."

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: That doesn't sound frightening.

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: It will.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Remember that name. The soft part. We'll be back.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The walls were one problem. The other was the Pope. Rome would send help, but only if the Greek Church agreed to join the Catholic one. On the twelfth of December, fourteen fifty-two, that union was proclaimed in Hagia Sophia itself, with the emperor present.

lines.speaker: GENNADIUS
lines.text: You will lose the city! And your children will be sold as slaves!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That's the monk Gennadius, and he was, in the long run, not entirely wrong.

lines.speaker: CITIZEN
lines.text: Rome will send ships.

lines.speaker: CITIZEN
lines.text: Rome will send a bill.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: One chronicler claims plenty of people signed only because they planned to quietly undo it once the Turks went home. Nothing brings a besieged city together like a theological argument, in the sense that everyone is furious at the same time.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Meanwhile, in Edirne, the Ottoman capital, a young man was making plans. Mehmed the Second was born in fourteen thirty-two. He was already a sultan once, briefly, as a boy. In fourteen fifty-one he took the throne again, and this time he meant it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: What was said in that council, we can only reconstruct. It probably went something like this.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: There is a narrow place on the Bosphorus. Six hundred and sixty meters. I want a fortress on it.

lines.speaker: HALIL
lines.text: My lord, with respect, that land belongs to the Greeks.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: Which Greeks?

lines.speaker: HALIL
lines.text: The ones with the city. The one we are… standing next to.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: Then they will not object. They haven't the soldiers.

lines.speaker: HALIL
lines.text: They will say it breaks a treaty.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: Then they will say it. Slowly. In writing.

lines.speaker: HALIL
lines.text: My lord, the last time you were sultan, you were twelve.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: And now I am nineteen.

lines.speaker: HALIL
lines.text: Twenty.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: Then I have even more experience than I thought.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Majesty. The sultan is building a fortress on the Bosphorus.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Where?

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: On the strait. Our strait.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: We have a strait?

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: We had one, Majesty. It is now under construction.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He built it fast. Begun in the spring of fourteen fifty-two, finished on the thirty-first of August, using stones taken from nearby churches. Its Turkish name was Boghaz-kesen. The strait-cutter. Or, if you prefer a more direct translation, the throat-cutter.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In November, a Venetian ship refused to stop for inspection, and was sunk. The captain, a man named Rizzo, was impaled. His sailors were beheaded. Their bodies were left by the road. The West had been telling itself the sultan was a boy who could be managed. After that, it stopped telling itself that.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Now the most expensive job interview in medieval history. A Hungarian engineer called Urban, who cast bronze cannon, arrived in Constantinople looking for work.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The chroniclers give us the outcome, not the dialogue. But the sequence of events was very close to this.

lines.speaker: URBAN
lines.text: Majesty. I make the biggest guns in the world. One shot, and the wall—

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: I have walls. I need a way to keep them.

lines.speaker: URBAN
lines.text: Then you will want a gun, to frighten the enemy.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Perhaps. What is your fee?

lines.speaker: URBAN
lines.text: Regular wages. Regular supplies. Regular bronze.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Bronze costs money.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: And so, regrettably, do you.

lines.speaker: URBAN
lines.text: Surely, for an emperor—

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: I can offer gratitude.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Gratitude is not on the payroll.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Urban went down the road to the sultan.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: How much do you want?

lines.speaker: URBAN
lines.text: Four times what the emperor offered, and—

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: Done.

lines.speaker: URBAN
lines.text: —with respect, my lord, I have not told you what it can do.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: Tell me.

lines.speaker: URBAN
lines.text: It can break the walls of Babylon.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: I'm not interested in Babylon.

lines.speaker: URBAN
lines.text: Of course. The walls of Constantinople, then.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: Better.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The gun was delivered toward the city in March, with sixty oxen pulling and two hundred men walking alongside to steady it, and two hundred more laying the road ahead.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: What's that noise?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Oxen.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: How many?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Sixty.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: What are they pulling?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Sixty oxen's worth of trouble.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In April, it slid off its platform in the mud. It could fire seven times a day.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Seven shots. A modern gunner would call that a long lunch. But each shot was a stone ball weighing hundreds of kilos, and each one left a hole.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The emperor, meanwhile, wanted to know what he had. He ordered a secret census of every man able to carry a weapon. It fell to the chancellor, George Sphrantzes, to count.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: I have the number, Majesty.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Say it.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Four thousand nine hundred and eighty-three.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Greeks.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Greeks. Plus the foreigners. Less than two thousand.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Under seven thousand, then.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: I counted twice.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Did it improve?

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: No, Majesty.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Keep it between the two of us.

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Majesty, who would believe me?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Under seven thousand men on a four-mile wall. And five miles away, sixty oxen were still pulling.
